subject.title: [Security] Missing audit trail and rate-limiting on sensitive plugin lifecycle hooks

question: Should OpenClaw treat this as defense-in-depth observability for trusted plugin operators, or establish a stronger authenticated remote-control boundary with mandatory actor attribution and rate limiting?
rationale: The current trust model, local CLI path, Gateway admin-scoped chat path, and install-policy hook have different actor and abuse semantics; choosing a cryptographic ledger, identity model, and throttling behavior is a security and product contract rather than a mechanical fix.

options.title: Narrow lifecycle auditing
options.body: Emit bounded structured attempt/result events for all mutation paths, reuse authenticated identity where available, and defer rate limiting until a concrete remote abuse path is demonstrated.

options.title: Full control-plane hardening
options.body: Define a durable actor model, tamper-evident or externally anchored audit storage, and per-principal rate limits across every remote plugin mutation surface.

options.title: Require exploit evidence first
options.body: Keep existing authorization and install-policy controls unchanged until a reproducible current-main boundary bypass identifies where additional enforcement belongs.

recommendation.title: Narrow lifecycle auditing
recommendation.body: Emit bounded structured attempt/result events for all mutation paths, reuse authenticated identity where available, and defer rate limiting until a concrete remote abuse path is demonstrated.
